references.text: The same motif that whoever eats the bread (Jesus' body) will live forever is expressed directly in the previous verse, where Jesus presents himself as the living bread that gives life to the world.
Jesus identifies himself as 'the Way, the truth, and the life', which supports the claim in 6:57 that life comes through him and that he is the source of life.

In the prayer before his suffering, Jesus confirms that the Father has given him authority over all flesh to give eternal life, defining eternal life as knowing the true God and Jesus Christ, whom he has sent.
Jesus explains that the Father has given the Son to have life in himself, parallel to 6:57 where Jesus says he lives 'because of' the Father, and that the Son gives life to those who eat him.
Jesus declares that he is the resurrection and the life, and that whoever believes in him will live even if they die, which mirrors the promise that whoever eats him will live forever.
The prologue establishes that life was in the Word (the Son) from the beginning, and that this life is the light for humanity, a theological foundation for the claim that Jesus is the source of life.
